Five simulated animals in Stoney Lake with known tracks

Source: R/data.R
stoney_track.Rd

The example study of the positionR packages: Stoney Lake, Ontario, on a 100 m depth raster, 70 receivers on a grid of 700 m steps with some of 600 m (nearest neighbour 600 to 922 m, median 700 m), and five animals walked for 48 hours from 00:00 UTC on 1 June 2024 with the correlated random walk of the arraydesign simulator (30 m a minute on average, step SD 15 m, turns of SD 40 degrees), each from a random water cell. Each tag transmits with a delay drawn uniformly from 120 to 180 s. Every transmission was detected or missed by each receiver with the probability of the Stoney example's range model: the logistic curve of de_logistic() with d50 250 m and d05 500 m at a receiver depth of 1 m and 750 m and 1,500 m at 35 m, read at the distance through water, with no variation between receivers or hours. A detection field built from that model with a spread of 0 is therefore the model the detections came from. The array is dense enough that 17% of the 212 detected animal-hours are heard by a single receiver.

Usage

stoney_track

Format

A list of six elements:

receivers

The receiver deployments, one row per receiver: receiver_serial, station_id, deploy_datetime, recover_datetime, deploy_lat, deploy_lon, deploy_z (receiver depth, 1.1 to 16.1 m, the depth of its cell), and the projected x and y in UTM zone 17N (EPSG:32617), with attr(, "epsg").

detections

3,641 detections: datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter and animal_id; 803 of stoney-01, 1,063 of stoney-02, 487 of stoney-03, 273 of stoney-04 and 1,015 of stoney-05.

tags

One row per transmitter: transmitter, animal_id, min_delay (120 s) and max_delay (180 s).

track

The true position each minute: animal_id, datetime, x and y, 2,881 rows per animal from 00:00 UTC on 1 June 2024 to 00:00 UTC on 3 June.

transmissions

Every transmission, heard or not: animal_id, transmitter, datetime, x, y, cell (the raster cell) and n_detections (receivers that heard it); 1,148 to 1,153 per animal.

truth

The values the study was simulated with: the range model (d50, d05, depth, station_hour), the walk (step_mean, step_sd, turn_sd, time_step), tag_delay and the seeds.

The depth raster is included as stoney_depth.tif, and the study as the files stoney_deployments.csv, stoney_detections.csv and stoney_tags.csv, in system.file("extdata", package = "detfield"). The raster stores depth as metres of zero or below, with land NA; take abs() before depth arithmetic or a depth map. 56 of its 4,818 water cells hold 0. vignette("detfield") reads the files, and vignette("positioning") scores the positions against the tracks.

Source

Simulated with the arraydesign simulator by https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detfield/blob/main/data-raw/stoney_track.R, which is in the repository and not in the installed package. The raster has the same grid and depths as depth_raster of positionR 1.7.0, a 100 m depth raster of Stoney Lake, derived from the bathymetry made before 2024, with the CRS set to EPSG:32617. The arraydesignR app carries the same file.

See also

stoney_range_test for the range test of the same range model.

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000)
truth <- stoney_track$truth
model <- de_model(de_logistic(truth$d50, truth$d05, depth = truth$depth),
                  sigma = list(station_hour = 0))
field <- de_field(dist, model)
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
# Position one animal, to keep the example short
one <- stoney_track$detections[stoney_track$detections$animal_id == "stoney-01", ]
counts <- bin_detections(one, stoney_track$receivers, stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field, overdispersion = "none")
head(attr(credible_region(surface), "summary"))
#>   animal_id           bin_start n_cells area_m2      mass
#> 1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00      19  190000 0.9592477
#> 2 stoney-01 2024-06-01 05:00:00       5   50000 0.9803368
#> 3 stoney-01 2024-06-01 06:00:00       3   30000 0.9674755
#> 4 stoney-01 2024-06-01 07:00:00       5   50000 0.9850715
#> 5 stoney-01 2024-06-01 08:00:00       3   30000 0.9620796
#> 6 stoney-01 2024-06-01 09:00:00      16  160000 0.9581671
